recipe_story: This entry started as a tailgate chili and picked up a smoky incident-response personality over two cook-offs.
ingredients:
2 lb smoked chuck roast, cubed
2 cans fire-roasted tomatoes
2 cans pinto beans, drained
1 large onion, diced
3 cloves garlic, minced
3 tbsp chili powder
1 tbsp cumin
1 tsp smoked paprika
Salt and black pepper to taste
instructions:
Smoke the chuck roast until it reaches 165 F, then cube it.
Saute the onion and garlic until soft.
Combine everything in a Dutch oven or slow cooker.
Simmer until the beef is tender and the chili thickens.
Taste, tune the seasoning, and serve hot.
hack_story: The trick is treating the meat like packet capture: collect smoke early, inspect the texture often, and only merge it into the pot when the bark has useful signal.
serving_notes: Serve with sharp cheddar, pickled jalapenos, and corn chips.
allergens: Contains dairy if served with cheese.
